clue.text: Private has to be mad to accept mission

indicators.note: to accept is to take something in, so the mission sits inside the phrase for being mad

parts.note: to see red is to be furious
a quest is a mission or expedition

explanation.surface: A soldier must be crazy to agree to take on a dangerous mission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' looks like the soldier but is the definition; 'to be mad' is the idiom for flying into a rage, opened up by 'accept'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sequestered means secluded or kept apart, a synonym of private in the sense of hidden away.

clue.text: 11 dn's definition initially supports it

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece that supports another sits beneath it, so the initial comes last

parts.note: it is an old slang term for sex appeal, abbreviated SA

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word definition

explanation.surface: A cross-reference saying another clue's definition holds this one up.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition of 11 down (CRESTFALLEN) is 'Low', which means unhappy. 'it' as SA (sex appeal) is a crossword convention; in a down entry D supporting SA puts D under it.
explanation.definitionFit: The defining word of the other clue is low, which in the sense of downcast is a synonym of unhappy.

clue.text: Minimum attendance halved — oddly, they quantify the damage

indicators.note: halved means only the front half of the word for minimum attendance is used

parts.note: a quorum is the minimum number of members needed for a meeting to proceed

indicators.note: oddly signals the letters in odd positions of the word they

explanation.surface: Insurers count heads at a meeting before assessing the losses.
explanation.walkthrough: QUORUM halved gives QUO; the first and third letters of 'they' give TE.
explanation.definitionFit: To quote is to give an estimated price for a job, as a repairer does when costing damage.

clue.text: Always spread grass so it will dry inside-out

parts.note: ever means always, as in ever hopeful

parts.words: spread grass so it will dry
parts.note: to ted is to turn and spread mown grass for haymaking

explanation.surface: A farmer keeps turning the hay so it dries right through.
explanation.walkthrough: TED is a farming verb: to spread out cut grass so it dries into hay.
explanation.definitionFit: Everted is a technical term for turned outward, which is to say turned inside out.

clue.text: Move one's parts?

parts.note: read as rearranging the pieces of something, like swapping letters or shifting music into another key

explanation.surface: An actor asks whether they should shift their roles around.
explanation.definitionFit: To transpose is to change the order or position of parts, or to move music into another key.

clue.text: Shining light of manmade fibre

parts.note: a ray is a beam of light
a light that is shining is on

explanation.surface: Someone praises a glossy synthetic fabric as a beacon among textiles.
explanation.walkthrough: The charade is read in answer order: RAY (light) then ON (shining, as a lamp is on). 'of' joins wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rayon is a synthetic textile made from regenerated cellulose, an early manufactured fibre.

clue.text: Downgrade official position in a bad way

parts.note: a desk is a post or department in an office, as in the news desk
ill means unwell, in a bad way

explanation.surface: A civil servant's post is demoted in an unpleasant manner.
explanation.definitionFit: To deskill is to reduce the skill a job needs, a kind of downgrading of the work.

clue.text: Fill me with drink and I'll believe anything

definitions.meaning: a drinking vessel speaks: a cup with a handle that you fill
a gullible person, an easy dupe, speaks

explanation.definitionFit: A mug is both a large cup and, in slang, a person who is easily fooled.

clue.text: Second one trapping part of leg still makes it

parts.note: mo is short for moment, a second

indicators.note: trapping means the word for one holds the leg part inside it

parts.note: taken as written
the shin is the front of the lower leg

explanation.surface: A runner trips over again and is left motionless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' looks like an adverb but is the distillery apparatus that makes illicit spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonshine is illicitly distilled liquor, the product of a hidden still.

clue.text: Giant diesel loco set

indicators.note: loco means crazy, so these letters go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A huge diesel locomotive is ready to depart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loco' looks like a locomotive but is the anagram signal, slang for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelatinised means turned to a jelly, which is to say set like jelly.

clue.text: Domesticated now, this roamed wild in desert conditions

definitions.text: Domesticated now, this roamed wild in desert conditions

indicators.note: in puts the scrambled letters inside the word for desert conditions

parts.note: desert conditions are dry

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters run loose into a new order

explanation.surface: A creature now tamed once wandered freely through arid lands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' turns 'roamed' into a new order, and 'in' puts that inside the word for arid. The whole clue describes the one-humped camel, now almost only domesticated.
explanation.definitionFit: The one-humped camel of Arabia is now known almost only in domestic herds.

clue.text: Lower hood after start of service

indicators.note: after places the hood after the opening letter
start of means only the opening letter of the word service is taken

parts.note: a cowl is a monk's hood

explanation.surface: A monk drops his hood once the church service begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' reads as 'lower down' but is lour, to frown.
explanation.definitionFit: To lower or lour is to look sullen and frown, the same as to glower.

clue.text: Chests full of English coins

indicators.note: full of means the boxes contain the abbreviation inside

parts.note: crates are large boxes or chests

explanation.surface: Treasure chests packed with English money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coins' looks like a noun but is the verb: to coin a phrase is to invent it.
explanation.definitionFit: To coin a word is to invent it, so coins means makes or originates.

clue.text: Low Conservative support? Slough gets everyone on board

parts.note: a rest is a support, as for a snooker cue

indicators.note: on board means taken inside, so the word for everyone sits within the boggy ground

parts.note: a slough is a swamp, and a fen is marshland
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A Tory campaign flops in Slough despite every voter being signed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slough' looks like the English town but is a bog. 'gets' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling low means being dejected, and crestfallen describes someone downcast after a setback.

clue.text: Punch bag's stuffing is suffering

indicators.note: stuffing means the letters fill the inside of the bag

parts.note: a net is a bag of mesh
ails means is ill or suffering

explanation.surface: A boxer's punchbag is losing its stuffing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punch' looks like a blow but is the carpenter's tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail set is a small punch used to drive nail heads below a surface.

clue.text: Honoured, as it were, after drug fix

indicators.note: after places the honour after the drug letter

parts.note: E is short for the drug ecstasy
made a Member of the Order of the British Empire, playfully as a verb

explanation.surface: A celebrity honoured in the New Year list gets a drug fix.
explanation.walkthrough: MBE is a British honour (Member of the Order of the British Empire); 'as it were' allows MBE-ED as a made-up verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To embed is to fix something firmly in a surrounding mass.

clue.text: Way to break down Bolshevik crew

indicators.note: to break means the street abbreviation splits the word for down

parts.note: blue means down or depressed
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
a Bolshevik is a communist, a Red

explanation.surface: A path collapses beneath a crew of revolutionaries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crew' reads as a team but is the past tense of crow, to boast.
explanation.definitionFit: Crew is the past tense of crow, to brag, and blustered means talked boastfully.

clue.text: Area secured by soldiers, effectively home after 1984

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers
well means effectively, as in working well

indicators.note: secured by means the area letter is held inside the word for home

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: Troops guard a district and settle back home after a dystopian year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' means in the manner of: 1984 is the George Orwell novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Orwellian describes the surveillance state of the novel 1984, so it means in its style.

clue.text: Funny seaweed keeping one dry

indicators.note: keeping means the seaweed holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: wrack is seaweed cast up on the shore
I is the Roman numeral one
sec is the wine term for dry

explanation.surface: Comic seaweed that somehow stays dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny' is the noun, a joke, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A funny as a noun is a joke, and a wisecrack is a witty remark.

clue.text: It's awful breaking stones in bits for grit

indicators.note: breaking means the exclamation splits the scrambled stones
in bits means the stones are broken into a new order

parts.note: ugh is an exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: A labourer complains while smashing stones into gravel.
explanation.walkthrough: TONESS, the anagram of STONES signalled by 'in bits', is broken by UGH.
explanation.definitionFit: Grit as courage or resolve is the same quality as toughness.

clue.text: Banal words of wisdom that metalworker may use?

parts.note: hack means trite or unoriginal, as in hack writing
a saw is a proverb or saying

explanation.surface: A trite proverb that a metalworker might quote at work.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacksaw is a fine-toothed saw for cutting metal, a staple of the metalworking trade.

clue.text: Railroad, a forerunner of ship?

parts.note: pre is the prefix meaning before, which comes ahead of a word
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A train line asks if it came before ships in transport history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Railroad' is the verb, to force someone into something.
explanation.definitionFit: To railroad someone is to press or force them into acting.

clue.text: Baby gets nothing for wind

parts.note: to baby someone is to pamper them
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An infant gets nothing but gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind' suggests a baby's burping but is a South American weather wind.
explanation.definitionFit: The pampero is a cold wind blowing across the pampas of Argentina.

clue.text: It can appear false in commercial for heartburn remedy

indicators.note: in puts the scrambled letters inside the advertisement

parts.note: an ad is a commercial

indicators.note: appear false means the letters are faked into a new order

explanation.surface: A television advertisement for an indigestion cure may not be truthful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appear false' rearranges 'It can', and 'in' puts the result inside the commercial. 'can' looks like part of the verb phrase but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An antacid neutralises stomach acid and is taken to relieve heartburn.

clue.text: Figure work on edges of instrument

parts.note: to dig is to work the soil

indicators.note: edges of means the outer letters of the word instrument

explanation.surface: A musician practises scales along the rim of their instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A digit is a single numeral, a figure from nought to nine.

clue.text: Direct, at first not direct

parts.note: the punctuation mark printed after the first word supplies its own name

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letters of the two words following

explanation.surface: An instruction contradicts itself: be direct, but begin by not being direct.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed comma after 'Direct' is itself part of the wordplay; ND are the initials of 'not direct'.
explanation.definitionFit: To direct someone is to command or order them.

clue.text: A pest regularly without welcome!

indicators.note: without means outside, so the alternate letters wrap the greeting
regularly means every other letter of the word pest

parts.note: hi is a word of welcome

explanation.surface: An unwanted pest arrives without any greeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the first and third letters of pest, and 'without' wraps them around the greeting. The whole clue also describes the greenfly as an unwelcome visitor.
explanation.definitionFit: An aphis is an aphid, the greenfly that infests garden plants.

clue.text: See runs and boundaries from deliveries here

definitions.text: See runs and boundaries from deliveries here

parts.words: See runs and boundaries from deliveries here
parts.note: read as a cricket venue where you watch batsmen score from bowled balls

explanation.surface: A spectator is told where to watch runs and fours being scored.
explanation.walkthrough: LORD'S is the London cricket ground. In cricket, deliveries are balls bowled and boundaries are fours and sixes.
explanation.definitionFit: The ground in St John's Wood is the home of cricket, where scoring from the bowling is watched.

clue.text: Right to wear goggles before baking wild slugs?

indicators.note: before puts the first piece ahead of the heat
to wear means the goggling word goes round the right letter

parts.note: to goggle is to stare open-mouthed, to gape
baking means very hot

explanation.surface: A gardener in goggles is baking wild slugs in the heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slugs' look like garden pests but are lumps of metal shot; GAPES wears R.
explanation.definitionFit: Grapeshot is a cluster of small iron balls fired from a cannon, scattering wildly like stray bullets.

clue.text: Eight, nine and eleven finally filling the gap

definitions.text: Eight, nine and eleven finally filling the gap

indicators.note: finally means the closing letter of each of the three number words

explanation.surface: A sequence of numbers is missing the one between nine and eleven.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letters of the three words spell the number that sits between nine and eleven.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing whole number between nine and eleven completes the count.

clue.text: Never a tip for deep sleep

parts.note: never a means not a single one, or no

indicators.note: tip for means the first letter of the word deep

explanation.surface: Advice that there is no hint for falling into a deep sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: The land of Nod is sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Nod is a short sleep or doze, as in to nod off.

clue.text: Handled at least twice, maybe more?

definitions.text: Handled at least twice, maybe more?

parts.words: Handled at least twice, maybe more?
parts.note: read as having handles fitted plural times, and the idiom for something even more so

explanation.surface: Something gripped by the hand two or more times.
explanation.walkthrough: The British idiom means 'and even more so'; knobs are handles, so the phrase is read literally too.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means the same and even more so, while knobs are handles fitted to something.
